_meta.feastLabel: Holy Pentecost — The Descent of the Holy Spirit

_sources.role: irmoi, troparion, magnification, prokeimenon, gospel, post-gospel sticheron, exapostilaria, lauds
_sources.label: OCA service text

_sources.role: sessional hymns, canon troparia, ikos, katavasia text
_sources.label: St-Sergius Pentecostarion (yy register)

_meta._note: Two-canon feast (1st by Cosmas of Maiuma Tone 7, 2nd by John Arklas / John of Damascus Tone 4). OCA publishes only the heirmoi for both canons; troparia + sessional hymns sourced from St-Sergius Pentecostarion. The assembler renders interleaved by canon group when troparia carry canon: 'secondCanon' tags. Magnificat is NOT sung at Pentecost per Pentecostarion rubric (skipMagnificat: true). Mixed translation registers — irmoi/lauds OCA tt, troparia/sessional hymns St-Sergius yy/archaic.

troparion.text:
Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God,
Who hast revealed the fishermen as most wise
by sending down upon them the Holy Spirit,
and through them Thou didst draw the world into Thy net.
O Lover of Man, glory to Thee!
troparion.label: Troparion of Pentecost

sedalion.text:
Let us, O ye faithful, radiantly celebrate that which followeth the former feast,
and is the concluding feast;
that is, the day of Pentecost,
the fulfillment of the promise and of the appointed time,
for thereon the fire from the Comforter came down upon earth,
as it were in the form of tongues,
and enlightened the disciples,
making them participants in heavenly things.
The light of the Comforter//
hath come and enlightened the world.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 1)

sedalion.text:
The well-spring of the Spirit, coming to earth,
noetically divided into rivers of fire,
and bedewed the apostles, enlightening them;
and He was to them a bedewing cloud,
a fire enlightening them, a flame raining down.
Through them we have received grace, through fire and water.//
The light of the Comforter hath come and illumined the world.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 2)

magnification.refrain:
We magnify Thee,
O Christ, the Giver of life,
and we honor Thy most-holy Spirit,
Whom Thou didst send from the Father
onto Thy divine Disciples.
verses: The heavens are telling the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims His handiwork. (Ps. 18:1)
And all the host of them by the Spirit of His mouth. (Ps. 32:6b)

sessionalHymns.text:
After Thine arising from the tomb, O Christ,
and Thy divine Ascension to the height of heaven,
Thou didst send down Thy glory upon the God-seers, O compassionate One,
having renewed a right spirit in Thy disciples.
Wherefore, like a musical harp plucked with a divine plectrum,//
they have mysteriously made clear Thy command, O Savior, and Thy dispensation.
sessionalHymns.label: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleios

prokeimenon.refrain: Thy good Spirit shall lead me into the land of righteousness!
prokeimenon.verse: O Lord, hear my prayer, consider my supplication.

gospel._note: "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ…" is NOT sung at Pentecost Matins; Psalm 50 is chanted at once.

postGospelSticheron.text:
O heavenly King,
the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth,
Who art everywhere and fillest all things;
Treasury of blessings
and Giver of life,
come and abide in us,
and cleanse us from every impurity,
and save our souls, O Good One!
postGospelSticheron.label: Idiomelon of Pentecost

canon._canonNote: Two canons in two tones. Troparia from St-Sergius Pentecostarion (yy register); irmoi/katavasia text from OCA service text (tt register) where present, St-Sergius elsewhere.

ode1.irmos2:
After he was covered by divine darkness,
Moses, the slow of speech, proclaimed the divinely-written law.
After he purified the eye of his mind,
he beheld the "I AM" and was taught the knowledge of the Spirit,
Whom he honored in divinely inspired song.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
As of old Thou didst promise the disciples, O Christ Who didst send the Spirit Comforter,
Thou didst indeed shine forth light upon the world, O Thou Who lovest mankind.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
That which of old was preached by the Law and the prophets hath been fulfilled;
for today the grace of the divine Spirit hath been poured out upon all the faithful.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The pure and revered mouth spake: From you there shall be no separation, O My friends!
For, seated together upon the Father's most high throne,
I will pour out the Spirit, to enlighten them that desire abundant grace.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

ode3.irmos:
Thou didst say to Thy Disciples, O Christ:
"Remain in Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.
And I will send you another Comforter, like unto Me.
He is My Spirit and the Spirit of My Father.
In Him you will be established."
ode3.irmos2:
Only the prayer of the prophetess Anna,
who of old brought a broken spirit unto the mighty One and God of knowledge,
loosed the fetters of a childless womb and the unruly rebuke of her with children.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The power of the divine Spirit coming down divinely joined together into one,
the divided tongues of those who of old had come to a wicked agreement,
thereby imparting unto the faithful the knowledge of the Trinity, in which we are established.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Incomprehensible is the supreme Godhead,
for it hath shown the illiterate fishermen to be wise men
who with their speech stopped the mouths of the sophists,
and brought out of the deepest night countless peoples, through the brilliance of the Spirit.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
From unbegotten Light the all-effecting never-failing Brightness doth proceed,
Who now shineth forth the radiance one in nature, of the Father's power,
through the Son, unto the nations in the fiery voice on Zion.

ode3.katavasia: Only the prayer of the prophetess Anna…

sedalenAfterOde3.label: Sessional Hymn (after Ode 3)

ode4.irmos:
When the prophet perceived Thy coming in the last days, O Christ,
he cried out: I have heard of Thy might, O Lord,
that Thou hast come to save all Thine anointed ones.
ode4.irmos2:
O King of kings, even Thou Who art from the Only One,
O Word, Who comest forth from the only uncaused Father,
Thou, as our Benefactor, didst unfailingly send
Thy Spirit, Equal in might, unto the apostles, who sing:
Glory to Thy power, O Lord.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
He that formerly spake through the prophets, and was foretold in the law unto the imperfect,
the Comforter, the true God, doth become known today
unto the ministers and witnesses of the Word.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Bearing the sign of Divinity, the Spirit was distributed in fire upon the apostles,
and was manifested in strange tongues,
for the divine Power coming from the Father is absolute.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Having by word thrown open the divine laver of regeneration,
Thou, O Word of God, Compound Nature, dost bathe me with streams from Thine incorrupt, pierced side,
sealing with the fervor of the Spirit.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
All things bow their knees unto the Comforter, and unto the Son of the Father,
and unto the consubstantial Father, for in Three Hypostases they saw the true Being,
inaccessible, timeless, and one; for the grace of the Spirit hath shone forth light.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

ode4.katavasia: O King of kings, even Thou Who art from the Only One…

ode5.irmos:
The Spirit of salvation, O Lord,
Who was conceived in the loins of the prophets because of their fear of Thee
and was brought forth upon the earth,
doth purify the hearts of the apostles,
and is renewed in an upright manner in the faithful;
for Thy commandments are light and peace.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
This power that came down today is the Good Spirit,
the Spirit of the wisdom of God,
the Spirit that proceedeth from the Father, and through the Son hath appeared unto us the faithful,
presented in the holiness of His nature, unto those in whom He dwelleth, and in whom He is seen.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
As He Himself was well-pleased, of His own accord the unsubordinated Spirit cometh forth from the Father,
making wise with tongues the apostles,
sealing with the impress of the life-bearing Word,
being of One Might with the Father, and One Form, of Whom the Savior spake also.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
That He might heal the minds of sin, the All-ruling God and Word
doth prepare for Himself as a spotless dwelling the apostles,
in whom the light of the Spirit, One in might and essence with Him, doth now make Its abode.

ode5.katavasia: O ye children of the Church…

ode6.irmos:
Sailing in the tempest of the cares of life,
together with the ship I have been submerged by sins,
and cast to the soul-corrupting beast,
wherefore like Jonah I cry to Thee, O Christ:
Lead me up from the deadly abyss.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Of Thy Spirit hast Thou abundantly poured out upon all flesh, according as Thou hast said, O Lord,
and all things are filled with Thy knowledge,
for Thou, the Son, didst come forth from the Father immutably,
and the Spirit indivisibly proceedeth.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Do Thou renew within us, that we may for ever possess the right Spirit that we long for,
Who proceedeth from the Father always invisibly,
consuming the stains of hated matter and cleansing the filth of our minds, O Ruler of all.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
A long-desired dignity dost Thou establish for the apostles in Zion mindful of Thy coming, O Spirit:
the profession of the Word Begotten of the Father,
which swiftly exposed the cruel prattle of the heathens' babbling.

ode6.katavasia: Thou hast shown forth from the Virgin…

kontakion.text:
When the Most High came down and confused the tongues,
He divided the nations;
but when He distributed the tongues of fire, He called all to unity.
Therefore, with one voice we glorify the All-holy Spirit.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of Pentecost

ikos.text:
Grant speedy and steadfast consolation unto Thy servants, O Jesus,
when our spirits are become despondent.
Depart not from our souls when they be in afflictions,
nor be Thou afar from our minds when they be in tribulations,
but do Thou ever go before us.
Draw nigh unto us, draw nigh, O Thou Who art everywhere present;
and even as Thou wast ever with Thine apostles,
so also do Thou unite Thyself to them that long for Thee, O compassionate One,
that, being one with Thee, we may praise and glorify Thine all-holy Spirit.

ode7.irmos:
When they were thrown into the fiery furnace,
the holy youths sang a hymn
and thus changed the fire into dew.
They cried: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of our Fathers!"

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
While the apostles proclaimed the great divine things,
the unbelievers considered as drunkenness the working of the Spirit,
through Whom the Trinity becometh known, the one God of our fathers.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The indivisible Nature do we theologize in Orthodox manner:
God the beginningless Father, the Word and Spirit of the same authority,
and we cry: O God of our fathers, Blessed art Thou.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The divinely-inspired seer of visions, Joel, thundered forth a divine saying,
as if spoken by the Word of the supreme Godhead:
They on whom I will pour out my Spirit, shall exclaim together:
O Nature, splendid with the Triple Radiance, blessed art Thou!

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
At the third hour grace was seen to be well distributed,
that it might indicate the worship of Three Hypostases in a simplicity of authority,
but now we see in that unity on this, the Lord's day, the Son, the Father and the blessed Spirit!

ode7.katavasia: The harmonious music of the flutes sounded forth…

ode8.irmos:
The burning bush on Sinai was not consumed by fire,
but made God known to Moses, who was slow of speech and tongue.
And zeal for God made the three Youths immune to the fire
as they sang: "Praise the Lord, all His works;
highly exalt Him throughout all ages!"
ode8.irmos2:
The type of the Godhead prefigured in the resplendent three
loosed the bonds and moistened the flames with dew.
The children praise, and all creation that was made doth bless,
the only Savior and Creator of all, as their Benefactor.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
When the quickening mighty breath of the all-holy Spirit came down from on high
upon the fishermen in the form of tongues of fire,
they proclaimed the greatness of God:
All ye works, praise ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him throughout all ages.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Without dreading the fearful fire and like those treading up the untouchable mountain,
come, let us stand upon Mount Zion, in the city of the living God,
singing in choir together with the Spirit-bearing apostles:
All ye works, praise ye the Lord, and supremely exalt Him throughout all ages.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
The Spirit coming down in likeness of the tongues of fire,
doth impress upon the memory of the apostles the man-saving doctrine
which Christ Who heard it from the Father, declared unto them.
Creation, formerly alienated and now reconciled, doth praise Thee.

troparia.refrain: We bless Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, the Lord.
troparia.text:
O Light self-radiant and the cause of light, being alone self-mastering,
unto salvation hast Thou come filling the apostles, esteemed as the summit by Thy servants.
O that Thou shouldest grant the Spirit in great abundance!

troparia.refrain: Now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

ode8.katavasia: The type of the Godhead prefigured in the resplendent three…
ode8._katavasiaCloser: We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, praising and supremely exalting Him throughout all ages.

ode9.irmos:
Without knowing a man thou becamest a mother,
without knowing corruption thou didst bear a Child,
giving flesh to the Word, Who creates all things,
containing Him Who cannot be contained,
encompassing thine infinite Maker:
O Virgin Theotokos, we magnify thee.
ode9.irmos2:
Rejoice, O Queen, glory of mothers and virgins!
No tongue, however sweet or fluent, is eloquent enough to praise thee worthily.
Every mind is overawed by thy childbearing.
Therefore, with one voice, we glorify thee.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Borne in gladness upon a chariot of flaming fire,
the fire-breathing zealot of old typified that radiant breath
which now shone forth from above upon the apostles,
and these, illumined, made known the Trinity to all.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
troparia.text:
Strange things were heard from the disciples, not in accordance with the law of their nature,
for while only one voice spake, by the grace of the Spirit
various peoples, tribes, and nations heard the great things of God,
learning the knowledge of the Trinity.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.
Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
Let all of us, on whom the divinely-poured grace hath breathed,
shining, flashing, changed with a strange and most magnificent transformation,
having come to know the Essence equal in might, indivisible, and wise, and thrice radiant, render glory.

ode9.katavasia: Rejoice, O Queen boast of virgins and of mothers…

exapostilaria.text:
O All-holy Spirit,
proceeding from the Father,
and dwelling through the Son
in the unlettered Disciples,
save and sanctify all those who acknowledge Thee as God.
exapostilaria.melody: Thou didst cover the heavens with stars
exapostilaria.label: 1st Exapostilarion

exapostilaria.text:
The Father is Light, the Son is Light,
the Holy Spirit is also Light!
He was sent to the apostles in fiery tongues.
Through Him the whole world is enlightened
and adores the Holy Trinity.
exapostilaria.melody: Thou didst cover the heavens with stars
exapostilaria.label: 2nd Exapostilarion

stichera.verse: To execute on them the judgment written. This is glory for all His faithful ones. (Ps. 149:9)
stichera.text:
Today in the city of David
all the nations beheld glorious wonders,
when the Disciples of Christ had gathered together,
and the Holy Spirit came down in tongues of fire,
as Luke, inspired of God, records:
"A sound came like the rushing of a mighty wind;
it filled all the house where they were sitting,
and they all began to proclaim strange words, strange doctrines,
strange teachings of the Holy Trinity."

stichera.verse: Praise God in His sanctuary; praise Him in His mighty firmament. (Ps. 150:1)
Praise Him for His mighty deeds; praise Him according to His exceeding greatness! (Ps. 150:2)
Praise Him with trumpet sound; praise Him with lute and harp! (Ps. 150:3)
Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and pipe! (Ps. 150:4)
stichera.text:
The Holy Spirit is Light and Life,
a living Fountain of spiritual gifts,
the Spirit of wisdom and understanding,
all-knowing, upright and good:
He leads us and washes away our sins.
He is God, and He makes us gods;
He is Fire proceeding from Fire,
speaking and acting and distributing gifts.
Through Him all the Prophets, Martyrs and Apostles of God are crowned.
Strange account, strange and wonderful sight:
fire is divided for distributing gifts.

stichera.verse: Praise Him with sounding cymbals; praise Him with loud clashing cymbals! Let everything that breathes praise the Lord! (Ps. 150:5)

doxastikon.text:
O heavenly King,
the Comforter, the Spirit of Truth,
Who art everywhere and fillest all things;
Treasury of blessings
and Giver of life,
come and abide in us,
and cleanse us from every impurity,
and save our souls, O Good One!
doxastikon.author: Idiomelon of Pentecost

troparionAfterDoxology.text:
Blessed art Thou, O Christ our God,
Who hast revealed the fishermen as most wise
by sending down upon them the Holy Spirit,
and through them Thou didst draw the world into Thy net.
O Lover of Man, glory to Thee!
